content.content:
# Absys

**Evidence class: reconstructed.** No Absys implementation survives. The
system used is the reconstruction in https://github.com/chrishayuk/absys,
built from Foster (1968), Foster and Elcock (1969), Elcock (1982) and
Elcock (1990). Every rule it follows, and the evidence for each, is in its
`docs/decisions.md`.

## Pinning

The commit used is fixed when the specification is frozen. It is
`efd5203` (`PINS.md`): `7bb61e6` with one defect of the printer fixed.
Printing a list that contains itself (`x = [x]`, P01c) overflowed the
stack after the computation had finished. Only the printer changed, and
every example and research text prints byte for byte as at `7bb61e6`
(160 runs), which is kept as the behavioural reference. The defect is
recorded in the reconstruction's `docs/decisions.md`. Any later change to the
reconstruction, for whatever reason, makes a new configuration, reported
separately beside the pinned one. Mechanisms added after the freeze are
never counted as native in the pinned configuration.

## Decisions taken while the precursor experiments ran

The reconstruction was built while the experiments E01–E09 ran. P01–P08
come from those experiments. These rules of the machine were set or changed
because of them:

| rule in `docs/decisions.md` | what it decides | prompted by |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | a primitive relation returns for each of its variables bound, to the head of the list | Elcock 1982's printed list (E06), the precursor of P02 |
| 15 | an applied body takes the place of its literal | setdiff under first-in first-out selection (E02), the precursor of P06d |
| 18, 19 | a `not` or `set` that cannot yet be decided waits and is run again | permuting the student and setdiff texts (E02, E03), the precursors of P06 and P08 |
| 6 | an application of an identifier with no value waits for it, and outside a lambda every identifier is shared by the whole text | E90 p. 10 for the waiting; the sharing across the whole text was made general when permuting E03, the precursor of P08 |

Results on P02, P06 and P08 should be read with this in mind. Rules 10 and
15 rest on readings of the sources that the experiments helped to choose;
rules 6, 18 and 19 are partly decisions where the sources are silent.

## Configurations

| configuration | what it is | class |
|---|---|---|
| **absys** | the reconstruction's defaults | reconstructed |
| absys-depth-first | `--search depth-first`: the backtracking reading of Elcock (1982) | reconstructed, alternative reading |
| absys-wake-back | `--wake back`: returned relations appended, as the word of Elcock (1982) says | reconstructed, alternative reading |

## The core

The machine as `docs/decisions.md` describes it, in the pinned commit:
equality as a process, with suspension of equations between unknowns;
`lambda` procedures applied in any direction; `or`, distributed into
derivations; `not` and `set`; `key`; arithmetic as relations over
integers, taken up when two of three values are known; `tout`; and the
incremental acceptance of assertions. Nothing else exists to be imported,
so every Absys configuration has no external mechanisms.

## Notation

Absys is known in three notations: Absys 1 (1969), the 1982 paper's, and
the 1990 retrospective's. Absys 1 has arithmetic, and the 1990 notation has
`not` and `set`. The notation for each problem is fixed by a rule, not
chosen: the **earliest** notation that has every construct the problem
needs. A problem that needs constructs found in no single notation is
recorded as such, with the notation used.

**No comparisons.** The pinned reconstruction has +, −, · and ÷ as
relations, and no <, ≤, > or ≥, as calibration found. Three claims are kept
apart:

| claim | status |
|---|---|
| the pinned reconstruction has no comparison operators | established |
| the notations recovered from the sources show none | supported by the sources examined: Foster (1968), the extracts of Foster and Elcock (1969), Elcock (1982) and Elcock (1990) |
| historical Absys never had comparisons | **not established**. The full description of Absys-4 (Elcock and Gray, 1988) and the program itself have not been seen |

Expressibility is recorded per **sub-problem**, not per problem family. A
sub-problem that needs a comparison cannot be transcribed: P05's x > 1,
P09c's n > 5, P10d's x > 1, P11's x ≥ 2, P12's n > 0, P13a–d's range, and
P15d. The other sub-problems of the same problem are recorded on their
own. The rule for every system then applies (`SPECIFICATION.md`,
expressibility):

- where a reformulation without the comparison keeps the meaning on every
  input the problem and its variants use (replacing n > 0 by an enumeration
  of the finitely many values used, for instance), it is the program of
  record, *expressible with reformulation*;
- where it does not (calibration's range, with m > n replaced by
  m = n + 1 and m ≤ n dropped, which leaves an endless derivation), the
  sub-problem is *not expressible*, and the reformulation is a named
  variant.

**Output.** The baseline prints at most 32 elements of a list and 24
derivations. The instrumented commit `5450449` (branch `measure`) adds
`--full`, which prints both in full, so `observe()` can read every answer.
With no occur check, a computation can end with a cyclic value (P01c), so
`--full` detects a list cell met again while it is being printed, and
prints `↻` for "the enclosing list again": X = [1|X] prints `[1|↻]`,
X = [X] prints `[↻]`. Tests cover cyclic tails and heads, cycles through
two variables, long and partly known lists, and many derivations.
Against the baseline, its default output is identical in all 140 runs, and
`--full` output is identical in the 132 runs the baseline did not cut
short.

**A fault, found and fixed.** At `7bb61e6` the default printer overflowed
the stack on a cycle through a list's elements, X = [X]: the computation
finished, and printing its answer crashed. It was fixed on `main` as
`efd5203`, the pinned commit, which prints `[↻]` in every mode. The fault
is kept on record, in the reconstruction's `docs/decisions.md` and in
`PINS.md`. No result is taken from `7bb61e6`.

## Units

- **Step:** one step of the machine, as its `--steps` budget counts them:
  one equation or one literal elaborated in one derivation.
- **Alternative:** one derivation. All are live at once under **absys**.
  Under **absys-depth-first**, all are held too, but only the first is
  elaborated until it hibernates or fails, so the count is of derivations
  held, of which one is live.
  A derivation is not equated with a Prolog choicepoint, or with any
  other system's unit. Comparable counts come only from quantities a
  problem defines.
- **Store:** a vector, from `--measure` on the instrumented commit
  `f1a63aa` (branch `measure`; `5450449` adds `--full` and changes nothing
  measured). For each assertion it gives the value at
  the end and the peak, sampled after every step, so the peak is exact at
  the granularity of steps:

  | quantity | what it counts |
  |---|---|
  | derivations | live derivations of the top-level computation |
  | sub_derivations | derivations inside `not` and `set` computations |
  | variables | variables created, in every derivation. Derivations only gain variables, so for one derivation this is cumulative; it falls only when a derivation fails. It is listed, but it is not retained store in the sense the others are |
  | bindings | variables with a value |
  | susp_equations | suspended equations between two uninstantiated variables |
  | susp_applications | applications waiting for a definition or their key |
  | susp_relations | arithmetic and `tout` relations waiting for values |
  | susp_negations | `not` and `set` waiting to be decided or tried again |
  | pending | equations, literals and alternatives queued, not yet taken up |
  | term_nodes | nodes of bound values, counted in every derivation that holds them, without regard to sharing |

  term_nodes is a logical size, not memory. Derivations share structure,
  so the memory held is smaller.

The state is also sampled right after an assertion is added and before the
first step, so a peak at a stage boundary is not missed.

The instrumented commit changes nothing the machine computes on the texts
tested. That is observational equivalence over that corpus, not a proof
for every workload. With
`--measure` off and on, its output was identical to the baseline's, byte
for byte: 20 texts in 7 output modes (140 runs), full traces included,
and the JSON of all 20. This was checked against `7bb61e6`, and again
after the branch was rebased onto `efd5203`, with the same result; `--full`
output also matched wherever the baseline cut nothing short (132 runs). Measuring is slow, because the
whole state is read after every step. Step counts are unaffected; only
time is. Results report the baseline commit for behaviour and the
instrumented commit for store.

## The same computation

The reconstruction is incremental. Every stage is received into the same
session, with no reposing.

## Prior work, not results

The absys repository's experiments E01–E09 ran versions of P01–P08 before
this specification existed. They will be written again from the problem
files after the freeze.
# Questions on the specification, and the readings implemented

*Harness author, common part, wave 1, against `spec-1.0`. No frozen file
was changed. Each entry says what is open, the reading implemented in
`harnesses/`, and why. An amendment (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Amendments") can
settle any of them; until then, every system harness implements the
reading here.*

## Q1. Descriptions in `stages.json` without constants

The brief asks for each stage's description "quoted or closely
paraphrased from the problem file", and also for "no constants". Most
stages' information is mostly constants (z = 2, pick's facts, ⟨1,2⟩).

**Implemented:** descriptions paraphrase the problem file with every
constant of the stage information replaced by a placeholder: `<k>` an
integer, `<atom>`, `<seq>` a sequence, `<facts>` a set of facts. The
names of unknowns and relations, and structural numbers fixed by the
problem rather than by its constants (sizes n, j = ⌈n/2⌉, m = n/4, the
four contributors), are kept. The line number points to the full text.
*Why:* the harness must not hold, or be able to pass, a stage's
information (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Writing a program", rule 6); the
constants are public in `problems/`, but a structure file that carried
them would invite a harness to supply them, and would be wrong for the
hidden variants.

## Q2. The command line has no place for size, order or answer mode

`run CONFIGURATION PROBLEM SUBPROBLEM MODE PROGRAM OUTDIR` names one
sub-problem, but P02b (six orders), P07a (six orders), P09a (two spawn
orders), P12 (n = 8, 12, 16; all and any one), P13 (four n) and P16
(three n; P16a also three arrival orders) are each several runs.

**Implemented:** SUBPROBLEM is an **instance id** from `stages.json`. A
sub-problem with one instance keeps its own id (`P07c`); the others name
their parameters (`P02b.R2R1R3`, `P07a.312`, `P09a.BA`, `P12c.n16.any`,
`P13d.n10000`, `P16a.n1000.interleaved`). P07a's instance in the written
order keeps the id `P07a`. The harness passes the instance's parameters
to the program; they are structure, not constants, since
`variants/README.md` says sizes and arrival orders were not varied.

## Q3. What a stage's query is

The problem files give the information of each stage and its valid
outcomes, but rarely a separate query. `PROTOCOL.md` says `answers(cap)`
is called at each stage.

**Implemented:** each stage poses one query per computation: the answers
to all the information of stages 1 to k, over the sub-problem's unknowns
(listed by name in `stages.json`), with cap 1 where the problem says
*any one* (P11 throughout, line 15; P12's any-one instances; P15a1,
P15b, P15b2, P15c) and 20 otherwise. The P11 stages before and after the
commit are any-one queries too, since P11 says its queries are for any
one outcome. P06e1 and P06e2, ground queries, are cap 20: they are not
*any one* queries.

## Q4. P16b: whose answers at stage 1, and whose budget

P16b's stage 1 is four spawned contributors, but its valid outcome is
joint (xᵢ = x₁ + i − 1), and only stages 2 and 3 are said to be "posed to
the shared instance … with one budget per stage for the whole".

**Implemented:** at stage 1 each contributor C1–C4 is spawned with its own
query (cap 20), its own budget and its own execution state, as for any
spawned computation (`PROTOCOL.md`: each separate computation has its own
budget); the joint state is read by `observe()`, and the classifiers
classify on it. Stages 2 and 3 are posed to `main`, the instance's top
level, with one budget. Where the configuration cannot share unknowns
between computations, stage 1 is one conjunction in `main`
(`spawn_fallback`, `fallback_queries`), as line 47 says. Whether a
configuration can share unknowns between computations is stated by its
system harness.

## Q5. P09b's order

P09a is posed in both orders; P09b says nothing of order.

**Implemented:** P09b is spawned once, in the order written (A, then B).

## Q6. How restart cost is measured, and so a reposed budget

`PROTOCOL.md` gives a reposed run a budget of "its measured restart cost
plus 10⁶", and `METRICS.md` defines restart cost as "the step count of
running stages 1 to k−1 alone, measured". It does not say whether that
run includes collecting stage k−1's answers, nor which run measures it.

**Implemented:** the restart cost is always measured, in the system's
step unit, and the budget of a reposed stage k is always that plus 10⁶
(10⁸ for P12, P13, P16):
- **in-run**, by default: the harness reads the system's step count at
  the moment stage k is first posed in the reposed run, after the replay
  of stages 1 to k−1 (each replayed stage having the budget it had when
  first posed). That count is the restart cost; the stage then runs on
  with 10⁶ more steps. In a configuration that poses stages 1 to k as one
  conjunction, "first posed" is the first entry into stage k's part,
  marked by the program's H call for it; work done after backtracking
  into earlier stages counts in the stage, not in the restart cost;
- **separate-run**, only where the system cannot read its count at that
  moment: stages 1 to k−1 are run alone first, posed as in the replay,
  without `answers()`, and their steps are the restart cost.

`restart_cost_method` records which. A reposed stage with no measured
restart cost is invalid (`validate.py`), except in a configuration that
has no step count at all (ALGOL 60 x1sim), whose records say
`budget_enforced: false` and `restart_cost: null`, as in Q12. *Why:*
`PROTOCOL.md` requires the measured restart cost plus the budget, so the
budget cannot fall back to the budget alone; in-run measurement measures
the replay actually spent, without an extra run.

## Q7. What follows a timeout, and how the rerun is posed

`PROTOCOL.md` says what follows *budget* and *error*, and that a stage
stopped by the safety limit is rerun once, but not how the rerun is posed
in an incremental configuration, nor how stage k+1 is posed after a final
*timeout*.

**Implemented:** a safety-limit stop kills the computation (the harness
cannot continue what it stopped from outside), so: the rerun of stage k
is a reposed run of stages 1 to k under the raised limit (attempt 2,
`reason: "safety-rerun"`), with the reposed budget; and after a final
*timeout*, stage k+1 is posed by reposing stages 1 to k+1
(`reason: "after-timeout"`), counted under restart cost, as after
*error*. A system harness that can stop a stage at the limit without
losing the computation (an engine it can abort and keep) says so, and
may then rerun incrementally.

## Q8. The scope of the effects log, and which runs write to it

`PROTOCOL.md` says effects are written to "one log per problem, never
reset, across every run the harness makes for classification", and that
separate observation runs write to a separate log. P11 judges L "when the
problem ends", and gives each of P11a–d its own valid L.

**Implemented:**
- one classification log **per configuration and instance** (P11a, P11b,
  P11c, P11d each), since each sub-problem's effects class is judged on
  its own L;
- behaviour runs write to it, their reposed stages and safety reruns
  included. Cost and storage runs, which are not used for classification,
  write to the observation log with the separate observation runs;
- never reset, even when the same instance is run in behaviour mode a
  second time (after a harness fault, for instance). Each record carries
  `entries_before_run`, so the classifiers can see what an earlier run
  left in L. Whether such a log can still be judged *exact* is theirs to
  say.

## Q9. "One identical stub for every system"

P11 says the harness provides L and emit "as one identical stub for every
system". The four systems cannot run the same code.

**Implemented:** the stub is identical in behaviour and in its log format
(`README.md`, section 6): append m, rendered as the system renders it,
with its run, stage, attempt and replay context; never fail, defer,
buffer past the stage, deduplicate or read. Each system harness binds it
into its language and lists that binding's tokens as H.

## Q10. P13's "larger values of n are not run after it"

P13 says a run stopped by either limit is recorded and the larger values
of n are not run after it. A run of the harness is one instance (one n),
so `run` cannot apply it. P12 and P16 take P13's *limits* ("as in P13")
but do not repeat this rule.

**Implemented:** the rule is applied by whoever runs the batch, across
runs, for P13 only (`stages.json`: `stop_larger_n_after_limit` on P13
alone), per configuration, task and mode, and an n not run is recorded
as not run. P12 and P16 run every n. *Why:* the text states the rule
under P13's own budget section; extending it is an amendment.

## Q11. No rerun in P12, P13 and P16

`PROTOCOL.md` reruns a stopped stage once with the limit raised tenfold;
P12, P13 and P16 fix their limit of 600 s and say it is not raised.

**Implemented:** in those three, the first stop is final
(`safety_limit.action = "fixed-limit-timeout"`, state *timeout*); there
is no second attempt (`rerun_limit_s: null`). The problem's own text is
the more specific.

## Q12. A budget that cannot be enforced (ALGOL 60, x1sim)

x1sim is behaviour only and reports no step count, so 10⁶ steps cannot be
enforced.

**Implemented:** its records say `budget_enforced: false`, only the
safety limit stops it, and no stage of x1sim can be *budget*. Its
non-terminating stages are therefore *timeout*, which is to be read as
the absence of a budget, not as evidence about the time taken.

## Q13. What the safety limit times in a reposed stage

"60 seconds per stage" does not say whether, in a reposed run of stages
1 to k, the replay of 1 to k−1 is inside the limit.

**Implemented:** the limit covers one attempt: the whole reposed run,
replay included, or, for an incremental stage, from posing stage k to the
end of `print()`. *Why:* the harness cannot tell from outside where a
replay ends in every system, and the limit protects the harness rather
than measuring.

## Q14. Execution state when answers are taken on a separate run

Where collecting answers would consume an incremental computation,
`answers()` and `observe()` are taken on a separate run of 1 to k; but
"the execution state is classified after the call", which is then on the
separate run.

**Implemented:** the execution state recorded is the one after
`answers()`, on whichever run it was called (`collected_on`). Whatever
the harness can read of the incremental computation's own state without
consuming it goes in that attempt's `notes`, with its source.

## Q15. P16d2's stage numbers

P16d2 is "P16d with stage 2 omitted and stage 3 replaced by xₙ = x₁", so
its stages could be numbered 1 and 3.

**Implemented:** they are numbered 1 and 2, consecutively, as every
harness poses them, and `stages.json` gives the file's number,
`file_stage: 3`, for stage 2.

## Q16. How the harness learns v at a commit stage

A reposed run "replays a commit as the information x = v, with the v
first selected", but nothing says how v reaches the harness.

**Implemented:** v is the commit stage's answer, from `answers(1)`,
verbatim. The harness passes that string back unchanged when it replays
the commit stage, and the program turns it into its information x = v.
The harness does not parse it. A system that selected nothing has
nothing replayed, and that is recorded. *Why:* anything else would have
the harness reconstruct an answer.

## Q17. Step counting in behaviour mode

Behaviour mode has "no instrumentation beyond the harness", but the
budget must be enforced, and in Python the budget and the step count are
the same `sys.monitoring` callback.

**Implemented:** the budget counter is part of the harness and runs in
every mode. Steps a behaviour run records incidentally are kept, but the
figures of record for steps come from the cost run (`README.md`,
section 8). Where a system harness's budget mechanism is itself the
instrumentation (Python), its README says so as a confound.

## Q18. What `print()` is

`PROTOCOL.md` lists `print()` among the operations without defining it.

**Implemented:** `print()` records the system's own rendering of what it
holds at the end of the stage, verbatim, distinct from `observe()`, which
records the state the observations need. The harness never reformats
either.

## Q19. Readings classified twice

P01c (finite and rational), P08 (closed and open) and P09d (P09d1 and
P09d2) are run once and classified under each of their readings. P15b and
P15b2 have one reading only, the stream reading of P09d2 with fairness
(problems/15 lines 25, 38–44), and `stages.json` lists that one.

**Implemented:** each is one instance and one run; `stages.json` lists
its readings; nothing in the harness depends on a reading.

22	## 1. The first principle
23	
24	**A harness observes what the system computes. It never supplies it.**
25	
26	A harness passes stages in, collects answers through the system's
27	standard mechanism for answers, reads state for `observe()`, enforces the
28	budget and the safety limit, and writes the record. It does not, on the
29	system's or the program's behalf:
30	
31	- suspend a computation, or wait for information;
32	- search, backtrack, or enumerate values;
33	- schedule, interleave or arbitrate between computations, or run
34	  computations concurrently itself (`PROTOCOL.md`: concurrency is a
35	  mechanism of the configuration);
36	- propagate constraints, or simplify, reconstruct, complete or combine
37	  answers;
38	- combine stages, work out the net information of a reposed run, or skip
39	  a replayed stage;
40	- order, choose, retry or re-pose goals on its own.
41	
42	Where a configuration lacks a mechanism, the harness does not make up for
43	it. The program must, as S code counted against that configuration, or
44	the problem is *not expressible* there. Everything a harness does beyond
45	passing stages in, collecting answers and reading state is listed in its
46	README as a possible confound, and copied into each record's
47	`run.confounds`.
48	
49	## 2. Terms
50	
51	| term | meaning |
52	|---|---|
53	| **instance** | one thing a harness runs: a sub-problem at one size, in one arrival or spawn order, in one answer mode. Its id comes from `stages.json` (`P01a`, `P02b.R2R1R3`, `P12c.n16.any`, `P13d.n10000`, `P16a.n1000.interleaved`). A sub-problem with one instance has the sub-problem's own id |
54	| **run** | one invocation of `harnesses/<system>/run`: one configuration, one instance, one mode, every stage of the instance in order. It writes one raw record |
55	| **stage** | as the problem file numbers it (`stages.json` gives the line). Stage k's information is held by the program, never by the harness |
56	| **computation** | `main`, the instance's one computation (or its top level); or a computation started with `spawn()` (P09a, P09b, P16b), named as `stages.json` names it |
57	| **attempt** | one try at a stage under the safety limit. A stage has one attempt, or two when the first was stopped by the safety limit and the problem allows a rerun |
58	| **query** | one call of `answers(cap)` on one computation at the end of a stage. Each stage of `stages.json` lists its queries with their caps |
59	
60	The query of a stage is always about all the information of stages 1 to k
61	(`SPECIFICATION.md`, "Stages and monotonicity"), over the sub-problem's
62	unknowns. `stages.json` lists those unknowns by name; their values are
63	for the classifiers.

65	## 3. How a run is driven
66	
67	    harnesses/<system>/run CONFIGURATION PROBLEM SUBPROBLEM MODE PROGRAM OUTDIR
68	
69	| argument | value |
70	|---|---|
71	| CONFIGURATION | a configuration of `systems/<system>/README.md`, by its name there (`absys-depth-first`, `plain`, `core`, `x1sim`, ...) |
72	| PROBLEM | `P01` … `P16` |
73	| SUBPROBLEM | an **instance id** from `stages.json`, which for a sub-problem with one instance is the sub-problem id (`P07c`), and otherwise names its parameters (`P12a.n8.all`). See `QUESTIONS.md`, Q2 |
74	| MODE | `behaviour`, `cost` or `storage` (section 8) |
75	| PROGRAM | the program's path, relative to the repository root |
76	| OUTDIR | where the raw record is written: `results/<system>/<configuration>/<problem>/raw/` (section 10) |
77	
78	Exit status: **0** when a valid record was written, whatever the run's
79	outcome (an *error*, *budget* or *timeout* stage is a result, not a
80	failure of the harness); **2** for a usage error (unknown configuration,
81	instance or mode; a mode the systems file does not allow for that
82	configuration, such as `cost` for *x1sim*), with no record written;
83	**3** when the harness itself failed and could not write a valid record.
84	A harness fault that still allows a record is written into
85	`harness_faults` and exits 0.
86	
87	**The harness runs inside that system's pinned Linux image**
88	(`sandbox/README.md`, `PINS.md`): `cp-systems:spec-1.0` (Absys, ALGOL 60,
89	x1sim), the pinned `swipl:11.0.1` image, the pinned `python:3.13.7`
90	image. It assumes nothing of the host. It needs only what the image has,
91	plus the repository mounted at a path it is given or finds from its own
92	location. It records the system build it ran (section 9). The launcher
93	outside the container (whatever starts it) is not part of the harness and
94	may not change what it does; it may pass the image digest in, by an
95	environment variable the system harness names, since the harness cannot
96	always read it from inside.

98	What `run` does, in this order, and nothing else:
99	
100	1. Read `harnesses/stages.json`; find the instance; take its stages, its
101	   queries and caps, its commit and spawn stages, and its limits (a
102	   problem's `limits`, else `default_limits`).
103	2. Check the program with nothing but reading its bytes (SHA-256) and,
104	   where the systems file needs it, the constants input (section 11).
105	3. For k = 1 … K: **pose** stage k (section 4); for each spawned
106	   computation of the stage, **spawn** it; for each query of the stage,
107	   **answers(cap)**; then **observe()** and **print()**; then record the
108	   attempt. Apply the safety limit (section 7); after a stop, rerun once
109	   where allowed.
110	4. Write the record, then validate it with `validate.py`. A record that
111	   does not validate is a harness fault (exit 3), kept beside the output
112	   under the name `<run_id>.INVALID.json`, never silently dropped.

119	by `run` (Q10).

121	## 4. The operations
122	
123	These are `PROTOCOL.md`'s, made concrete. A per-system harness implements
124	exactly these and nothing that orders, chooses or re-poses goals on its
125	own.
126	
127	### pose(stage)
128	
129	Gives the system the information of stage k, in one of two ways, chosen
130	by the configuration's systems file ("The same computation"), never by
131	the harness from results:
132	
133	- **incremental**: stage k is received into the computation that holds
134	  stages 1 to k−1 (an Absys session, a SWI-Prolog *session* engine, a
135	  Python or ALGOL 60 program that reads each stage from its input as it
136	  arrives). Recorded `posed.how = "incremental"`.
137	- **reposed**: a new computation is started, and stages 1 to k are
138	  replayed into it **in order, every one of them, replacements and
139	  withdrawals included** (P10, P15d). The program carries them out. The
140	  harness never works out the net information itself, never drops a
141	  stage that a later one replaced or withdrew, and never merges stages.
142	  Recorded `posed.how = "reposed"`, `posed.replayed = [1, …, k−1]`.
143	
144	Stage 1 is always `fresh`. What the harness gives the program is only:
145	which stage to pose (k), for a reposed run the list of stages to replay
146	(1 … k−1) and any replayed commitments (below), and the instance's
147	parameters (n, order, answer mode, as `stages.json` gives them). The
148	program holds the stage information. The harness never passes a constant
149	of a problem.
150	
151	**No anticipation** (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Writing a program", rule 5): the
152	harness tells the program about stage k only when stage k is posed, and
153	never tells it how many stages follow.
154	
155	### spawn(computation)
156	
157	P09a, P09b and P16b. Starts a separate computation **in the same
158	instance of the system**, sharing one database, never in a separate
159	operating system process (`PROTOCOL.md`). `stages.json` lists the
160	computations a stage spawns (`spawns`) and, for P09a, the order
161	(`spawn_order`).
162	
163	- Where the configuration can run computations side by side, `spawn`
164	  returns at once (`side_by_side: true`).
165	- Where it cannot, the first runs to its end or its budget, and then the
166	  next (`side_by_side: false`).
167	- Each spawned computation has its own budget and its own execution
168	  state, recorded separately.
169	- P16b only: where the configuration does not allow separate
170	  computations to share unknowns, the four contributions are posed as one
171	  conjunction in `main` (`spawn_fallback`), with `fallback_queries`, and
172	  that is recorded. Which configurations allow it is the systems file's
173	  and the system harness's statement, not the harness's judgement on a
174	  run.
175	
176	The harness may use the configuration's own mechanism for starting a
177	computation (an engine, a thread, a program's own spawn), as the program
178	asks for it. It may not interleave computations itself.
179	
180	### answers(cap)
181	
182	Collects the answers the system reports, **through its standard mechanism
183	for enumerating them** (each systems file says what it is; for Python and
184	ALGOL 60 it is the values the program prints), until the mechanism is
185	exhausted, the budget runs out, or `cap` answers have been collected.
186	`cap` is 1 for an *any one* query and 20 otherwise, as `stages.json`
187	gives it per query. The harness never asks for an answer the mechanism
188	did not offer, never filters or deduplicates answers, and never stops
189	early because the answers look complete. Each answer is recorded
190	**verbatim**, as the mechanism produced it, with `ended_by`:
191	
192	| ended_by | when |
193	|---|---|
194	| `exhausted` | the mechanism reported no more answers |
195	| `cap` | `cap` answers were collected; the mechanism was not asked again |
196	| `budget` | the budget ran out while collecting |
197	| `timeout` | the safety limit stopped the attempt |
198	| `error` | the system stopped with an error |
199	| `no-enumeration` | the configuration has no mechanism for asking for more: the program printed what it computed for the stage and the stage ended (Python, ALGOL 60) |
200

200	
201	The execution state is classified **after** the call (section 5).
202	
203	### observe()
204	
205	Records the state the common observations need (`SPECIFICATION.md`,
206	"Observations common to every problem"), **verbatim**, as the system or
207	the program holds it at the end of the stage, including at the moment a
208	budget runs out: bindings held (`SPECIFICATION.md`, "reported": a binding
209	is reported if `observe()` can read it), residual relations, suspended
210	work, alternatives held. `observe.raw` is what was read, unedited;
211	`observe.bindings` splits it by unknown only where that can be done
212	mechanically. A residual counts as reported only if it is state that the
213	system or program holds and acts on later; printing the posed information
214	back is not observing it, and the harness never makes a residual up from
215	the posed information.
216	
217	### print()
218	
219	The system's own rendering of what it holds at the end of the stage (an
220	Absys assertion's printed derivations, a Prolog toplevel's bindings, the
221	program's printed values), recorded verbatim in `print`. The harness
222	never reformats it.
223	
224	### Observing must not consume the computation
225	
226	In a configuration where collecting answers or observing would end or
227	alter the computation that the next stage extends (exhausting a
228	backtracking search in a SWI-Prolog *session* engine, for instance),
229	`answers()` and `observe()` for stage k are taken on a **separate run of
230	stages 1 to k**, and the incremental computation is left as it was. The
231	record marks each such query `collected_on: "separate-run"`, and the
232	observation `taken_on: "separate-run"`, and keeps the separate run's
233	stdout, stderr and steps under `separate_run`. Its P11 effects go to the
234	observation log (section 6). In a reposed configuration every stage's run
235	is already separate, and nothing more is needed.
236	
237	## 5. Execution state
238	
239	Recorded per computation, per attempt, in the vocabulary of
240	`SPECIFICATION.md` ("Execution state"), **as far as the harness can tell
241	it mechanically**:
242	
243	| state | what the harness reads to say so |
244	|---|---|
245	| `budget` | its budget mechanism fired (Absys `--steps`, `call_with_inference_limit/3`, the `sys.monitoring` callback, `--max-steps`) |
246	| `timeout` | the safety limit stopped the attempt |
247	| `error` | the system stopped with an error; the error is copied verbatim to `error_verbatim` |
248	| `alternatives pending` | the system's own report that a request for more answers would resume it (a nondeterministic exit, open choicepoints, hibernating derivations), or, for Python and ALGOL 60, the program's named pending structure, read by `observe()` |
249	| `suspended` | the system's own report of held work that later information may resume (suspended equations, attributed variables with goals, a blocked engine, a program's named queue) |
250	| `finished` | the system stopped and reports none of the above |
251	
252	`alternatives pending` and `suspended` may both hold. `finished` excludes
253	the others; at most one of `budget`, `timeout` and `error` holds. Where
254	the harness cannot tell mechanically, it says so (`determined: false`),
255	lists what it could tell, and gives its basis. **The harness never
256	classifies the semantic axis, the representation, the simplification or
257	the effects class**: those are the classifiers' (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Roles"),
258	from the record.
259	
260	## 6. Commitments and the effects log (P11)
261	
262	**Commitments are preserved when a run is reposed.** At a commit stage
263	(`stages.json`, `commit: true`: P11c stage 3, P11d stage 2), the system
264	selects one of its current outcomes, v, and reports it through its
265	answers mechanism (`answers(1)`). The harness keeps that answer verbatim.
266	When a later stage is reposed, the commit stage is replayed **as the
267	information x = v**, with v passed to the program verbatim as first
268	selected, and recorded in `posed.replayed_commitments`. The harness never
269	asks the system to select again, and never parses or rewrites v beyond
270	taking the answer as the system gave it. Where the system did not select
271	(one that keeps every alternative live), nothing is replayed as a
272	commitment, and that is recorded; the classifiers judge it as P11 says.
273	In P11a and P11b, which have one stage, the outcome is committed when it
274	is reported (`committed_when_reported`).
275	
276	**The effects log.** The harness provides L and emit: one stub, with the
277	same behaviour and the same log format in every system (the binding of
278	emit into each language is the system harness's).
279	
280	- `emit(m)` appends one entry, m as the program passed it, rendered as
281	  the system renders m, to the log, and returns. It does nothing else: it
282	  does not fail, defer, buffer past the end of the stage, deduplicate, or
283	  read the log. Nothing the system does can remove an entry.
284	- The log is a file of JSON lines, one entry per line, with the fields of
285	  `effect_entry` in the schema: `seq` (position, from 1, never reused),
286	  `entry`, `run_id`, `stage`, `attempt`, `during_replay_of` (the earlier
287	  stage being replayed when emit was called, in a reposed run, else
288	  null), and `log`.
289	- **One classification log per configuration and instance**, at
290	  `results/<system>/<configuration>/P11/raw/<instance>.effects.jsonl`,
291	  **never reset**, across every behaviour run the harness makes, reposed
292	  runs and safety reruns included. The record copies the entries this run
293	  appended into each attempt's `effects`, and the whole log after the run
294	  into `effects.log_after_run`, with `entries_before_run`.
295	- **Separate observation runs** (section 4) and **every cost and storage
296	  run** write to `<instance>.effects-observation.jsonl` in the same
297	  folder, which is not judged (Q8).
298	- Entries emitted while replaying an earlier stage carry
299	  `during_replay_of`, so that entries duplicated only by reposing can be
300	  counted separately. The harness marks when an entry was made; whether it
301	  is a duplicate, and whether it was before, at or after commitment, is
302	  for the classifiers.
303	
304	## 7. Budget and safety limit
305	
306	| | P12, P13, P16 | every other problem |
307	|---|---|---|
308	| budget | 10⁸ steps per stage and computation | 10⁶ steps per stage and computation |
309	| safety limit | 600 s per stage, **fixed, no rerun** | 60 s per stage, then **one rerun at 600 s** |
310	| source | the problem file (`stages.json`, `limits`) | `PROTOCOL.md`, "Running" |
311	
312	- **Steps** are in the systems file's unit (Absys steps, SWI-Prolog
313	  inferences, Python bytecode instructions, ALGOL 60 interpreter ticks).
314	  The budget is a classification within a system, never compared across
315	  systems. Each spawned computation has its own budget; P16b stages 2
316	  and 3 have one for the whole.
317	- **A reposed run** has a budget of its **measured restart cost plus
318	  10⁶** (10⁸ where the problem says). The restart cost is always
319	  measured, in the system's step unit, never estimated or taken from
320	  another run (Q6):
321	  - **in-run** (the default): the harness reads the system's step count
322	    at the moment stage k is first posed in the reposed run, after the
323	    replay of stages 1 to k−1. That count is the restart cost, and the
324	    stage then has 10⁶ more steps: its budget is the restart cost plus
325	    10⁶. During the replay each replayed stage has the budget it had
326	    when first posed (10⁶ each);
327	  - **separate-run**, only where the system cannot read its count at that
328	    moment: the harness first runs stages 1 to k−1 alone, posed exactly
329	    as in the replay and with no `answers()` call, and measures its
330	    steps; that is the restart cost, and the reposed run's budget is it
331	    plus 10⁶.
332	
333	  It is recorded in `steps.restart_cost`, with `restart_cost_method`
334	  (`in-run` or `separate-run`) and `restart_cost_source`. The only
335	  exception is a configuration with no step count at all (ALGOL 60
336	  x1sim, Q12), whose records have `budget_enforced: false` and
337	  `restart_cost: null`.
338	- **After budget.** If stage k ends in *budget* and the configuration can
339	  keep its computation and continue it, stage k+1 is posed into that same
340	  computation, with a new budget (`continued_after_budget: true`). Only
341	  where it cannot are stages 1 to k+1 reposed (`reason: "after-budget"`),
342	  counted under restart cost. Whether a configuration can continue is the
343	  system harness's statement, in its README.
344	- **After error.** Stage k+1 is posed by reposing stages 1 to k+1
345	  (`reason: "after-error"`), counted under restart cost, in every
346	  configuration, incremental ones included.
347	- **After timeout.** As after error: the stopped computation cannot be
348	  continued, so stage k+1 is reposed (`reason: "after-timeout"`), Q7.
349	- **Safety limit.** It protects the harness; it is not a measurement.
350	  It covers one attempt of one stage: for an incremental stage, from
351	  posing stage k to the end of `print()`; for a reposed stage, the whole
352	  run of stages 1 to k. When it stops an attempt, the harness stops the
353	  system by the means its README gives (`safety_limit.how_stopped`),
354	  records the attempt with what it had collected, and, where the problem
355	  allows, **reruns the stage once** with the limit raised tenfold
356	  (attempt 2, `reason: "safety-rerun"`). An incremental configuration's
357	  rerun is reposed, since the stopped computation is gone. If the rerun
358	  also stops, *timeout* is final for that stage (`final-timeout`). Under
359	  a fixed limit (P12, P13, P16) the first stop is final
360	  (`fixed-limit-timeout`). **Both attempts are recorded.** Answers
361	  collected before a stop are kept and classified on the semantic axis;
362	  only the execution state is *timeout*.
363	- A run that hits the safety limit only because it is instrumented (cost
364	  or storage, where the behaviour run finished) is recorded as such; it
365	  is not evidence about the model (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Modes of running").
366	  The classifiers read that from the records of the two modes.
367	- **ALGOL 60 x1sim** has no step count, so no budget can be enforced;
368	  only the safety limit stops it, and its records say
369	  `budget_enforced: false` (Q12).
370	
371	## 8. Modes
372	
373	Each program is run in up to three modes, one run each. A run's record
374	says its mode, and each figure is taken from the mode that gives it:
375	
376	| mode | instrumentation | gives |
377	|---|---|---|
378	| **behaviour** | none beyond the harness (its budget counter included) | answers, observe(), print(), the execution state, the effects log. **The semantic result and the execution state are taken from this run** |
379	| **cost** | step counting only | steps per stage (incremental and restated), restart cost, answer latency (steps to the first answer, between answers, to the end), problem operations, repeated work where the systems file names a source, candidates examined (P12) |
380	| **storage** | the systems file's storage measurement | store vector (boundary and peak), retained alternatives (at answers, at boundaries, at budget, peak), suspended state (at boundaries and peak), P13's maximum resident set size where the systems file takes it from a separate run |
381	
382	- **A sampled measurement is never taken from the run that gives the step
383	  count or the classification.** A sampled maximum (`peak.kind =
384	  "sampled"`) may appear only in a storage record; `validate.py` rejects
385	  one in a behaviour or cost record. Exact peaks may appear in any mode
386	  whose instrumentation gives them.
387	- A field a mode does not measure is `null`, or `{}` for the store
388	  vector. Figures that a mode records incidentally (the budget counter's
389	  steps in a behaviour run) are kept, but the figure of record is the one
390	  from the mode in this table.
391	- Where two modes can be compared, their answers must agree; a
392	  disagreement is reported as a fault of the instrumentation, by the
393	  classifiers, from the records.
394	- The systems file says which modes a configuration has (x1sim:
395	  behaviour only). P13's process CPU time and maximum resident set size
396	  are recorded where the systems file says, for growth only.
397	
398	## 9. The raw record
399	
400	One JSON file per run, valid against [`record.schema.json`](record.schema.json),
401	the same for every system. Every string the system produced is kept
402	**verbatim** (JSON-escaped, never trimmed, reflowed or decoded beyond the
403	system's own output encoding; bytes that are not UTF-8 are written as
404	`�` and noted in `harness_faults`). A value the harness could not
405	read is `null`, never estimated.
406	
407	### Run metadata (`run`)
408	
409	| field | what |
410	|---|---|
411	| `run_id` | unique, also the file's stem: `<instance>.<mode>.<UTC timestamp YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>` |
412	| `spec_tag` | `spec-1.0` |
413	| `system`, `configuration` | as in `systems/` |
414	| `problem`, `subproblem`, `instance`, `parameters` | from `stages.json`; `parameters` copied exactly |
415	| `mode` | behaviour, cost or storage |
416	| `purpose` | `primary`, `variant` (the verifier's), `qualification`, `example` (made up) |
417	| `program` | `path` and `sha256` of the program file as run, and the repository commit it was taken from |
418	| `constants` | `block`, `input` or `none`; the input file's path and SHA-256; the hidden variant's id when the verifier runs one |
419	| `system_build` | the pinned `commit` (from `/opt/src/COMMITS` in `cp-systems`), the `image` digest, the `binary`, the system's `version_output` verbatim, and whether the build or run is `instrumented` |
420	| `harness` | the harness's path, its git commit, and whether its files differed from it (`dirty`) |
421	| `command` | the harness command line as invoked |
422	| `posing` | `incremental` or `reposed`: the configuration's way of receiving a stage |
423	| `limits` | `budget_steps`, `step_unit`, `safety_limit_s`, `rerun_limit_s` |
424	| `started_utc`, `ended_utc`, `complete`, `incomplete_reason` | |
425	| `confounds`, `environment` | the system harness's listed confounds; environment it set (`PYTHONHASHSEED=0`, for instance) |
426	
427	### Per stage, per attempt (`stages[].attempts[]`)
428	
429	| field | what |
430	|---|---|
431	| `attempt`, `limit_s` | 1 under 60 s (600 s for P12, P13, P16); 2 for the rerun under 600 s |
432	| `posed` | `how` (`fresh`, `incremental`, `reposed`), `reason` (`first-stage`, `configuration`, `after-budget`, `after-error`, `after-timeout`, `safety-rerun`), `replayed` (the earlier stages replayed, `[1 … k−1]` when reposed), `replayed_commitments` (P11), `continued_after_budget`, `instance_parameters_passed` |
433	| `computations[]` | per computation: `id`, `spawned`, `spawn_index`, `side_by_side`; its `queries` (each with `id`, `cap`, `answers` verbatim with `steps_at` and `alternatives_at` where measured, `ended_by`, `collected_on`); its `execution_state` (`states`, `determined`, `basis`, `error_verbatim`); its `steps` (`unit`, `budget`, `budget_exhausted`, `budget_enforced`, incremental `stage`, `restated`, `restart_cost` with `restart_cost_method`, `to_first_answer`, `between_answers`, `to_end`, `repeated_work`); its `alternatives` in the systems file's unit (`at_boundary`, `at_budget`, `peak`, `held_as`: all live at once or kept for backtracking, `by_type`, `problem_defined`); its `suspended` work in the system's own terms (`at_boundary`, `peak`, `items` by kind with counts); `problem_operations` by relation case; `candidates_examined` (P12) |
434	| `observe` | `raw` verbatim, `method`, `taken_on`, `bindings` |
435	| `print` | verbatim |
436	| `store` | the systems file's vector, by quantity: `boundary`, `peak` (`exact` or `sampled`, with its interval) |
437	| `wall_time_s`, `cpu_time_s`, `max_rss_kb` | wall time (for the safety limit, not a metric); CPU and RSS for P13 growth only |
438	| `stdout`, `stderr` | verbatim, everything the system and program wrote during the attempt |
439	| `exit` | status and signal, or null where the process continues into the next stage |
440	| `safety_limit` | `hit`, `action` (`none`, `rerun`, `final-timeout`, `fixed-limit-timeout`), `how_stopped` |
441	| `effects` | P11: the log entries this attempt appended |
442	| `manual_actions` | every action by a person, or by code written for one problem, that the fixed harness does not perform (`METRICS.md`, "Intervention"), with who and why |
443	| `separate_run` | the separate run of stages 1 to k, where answers or observation were taken on one |
444	
445	At record level: `effects` (P11: the logs' paths and the whole
446	classification log after the run; null otherwise), `manual_actions`
447	outside any stage, `harness_faults` (what the harness itself failed to
448	do), `notes`.
449	
450	### Rules a record must keep (checked by `validate.py`)
451	
452	Beyond the schema:
453	
454	1. The instance exists in `stages.json`, with the same problem,
455	   sub-problem and parameters, and the problem's limits; a complete run
456	   has every stage, numbered 1 … K.
457	2. Each stage's queries are those of `stages.json`, on the computations it
458	   names, with its caps; spawned computations are those it spawns, in the
459	   instance's `spawn_order` (or the P16b fallback).
460	3. No query has more answers than its cap; `ended_by: "cap"` has exactly
461	   cap answers; `ended_by` budget, timeout or error appears in the
462	   computation's state.
463	4. Stage 1 is `fresh`. A reposed stage replays exactly 1 … k−1. An
464	   incremental stage replays nothing, and is not used in a reposing
465	   configuration except to continue after budget. After an error the next
466	   stage is reposed. A `continued_after_budget` stage follows a *budget*.
467	5. A reposed stage has a measured restart cost, with its method, and
468	   its budget is that plus the problem's budget; any other stage's is the
469	   problem's budget. Only a computation with `budget_enforced: false`
470	   may have no restart cost.
471	6. A second attempt exists only after the safety limit stopped the first,
472	   under the problem's rerun limit; none under a fixed limit. A *timeout*
473	   state and a safety-limit stop go together.
474	7. `finished` stands alone; at most one of budget, timeout, error;
475	   *error* has its text; *budget* matches `budget_exhausted`.
476	8. No sampled maximum outside a storage record.
477	9. A separate run, where one is used, replays 1 … k.
478	10. P11 records have `effects`; others do not. The entries of the
479	    attempts are exactly the classification log's entries after
480	    `entries_before_run`; cost and storage runs write only to the
481	    observation log; replayed commitments are for earlier commit stages.
482	
483	```
484	python3 harnesses/validate.py results/<system>/<configuration>/<problem>/raw/*.json
485	python3 harnesses/validate.py --check-stages            # checks stages.json itself
486	python3 harnesses/validate.py --stages harnesses/examples/stages-made-up.json harnesses/examples/made-up-*.json
487	```
488	
489	The last line runs on the made-up examples: three valid records (an
490	incremental run with a safety-limit rerun; a reposing run with a commit
491	and the effects log; two spawned computations in a storage run with a
492	separate observation run) and one deliberately invalid record, which it
493	rejects with six errors.
494	
495	## 10. Where records go
496	
497	    results/<system>/<configuration>/<problem>/raw/<run_id>.json
498	    results/<system>/<configuration>/P11/raw/<instance>.effects.jsonl
499	    results/<system>/<configuration>/P11/raw/<instance>.effects-observation.jsonl
500	
501	`OUTDIR` is that `raw/` folder. A harness never overwrites or deletes a
502	record: every run, including reruns, failed runs and runs on hidden
503	variants (`purpose: "variant"`, written under the verifier's own
504	`OUTDIR`), is kept. The result files of `PROTOCOL.md`, "Recording a
505	result" (`results/<system>/<configuration>/<problem>.md`) are written
506	from these records by the classifiers, and cite them by `run_id`.
507	
508	## 11. What a program must provide
509	
510	A program author cannot run anything before the program is fixed (only
511	the system harness's `check`, which executes nothing). So each system
512	harness's README says exactly, per configuration, how a program meets
513	these requirements; the common part is:
514	
515	1. **Stages as units the harness can pose.** The program handles stage k
516	   when, and only when, the harness poses it, in the way the
517	   configuration receives stages (incremental, or by replaying 1 … k).
518	   Code for stage k does not depend on any later stage.
519	2. **Replay.** In a reposed run the program carries out every stage
520	   1 … k in order, replacements and withdrawals included, and accepts a
521	   replayed commit stage as the information x = v, with v as the harness
522	   passes it (the verbatim answer of the commit stage).
523	3. **Instance parameters.** The program takes n, an arrival order, a
524	   spawn order or the answer mode from the harness, as `stages.json`
525	   names them, and holds everything else.
526	4. **Answers through the standard mechanism.** Answers reach the harness
527	   only through the configuration's standard mechanism for answers, in
528	   the form the system harness's README fixes (for Python and ALGOL 60,
529	   printed lines with the delimiters it defines).
530	5. **State for observe().** Whatever the system does not expose by
531	   itself (a Python program's named pending structure, its counters of
532	   problem operations), the program exposes in the form the system
533	   harness reads. Counters that only count are H (`METRICS.md`).
534	6. **Constants for the verifier** (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Writing a program",
535	   rule 6). Every constant of every stage is in **one** place the
536	   verifier can replace without touching anything else, and the program
537	   stays correct for other constants. Which place is fixed per system by
538	   its harness README, not here, with this default:
539	
540	   | system | where the constants are |
541	   |---|---|
542	   | ALGOL 60 | **input**: read with the input procedures as integers in the problem's encoding (`systems/algol-60/README.md`, "Values"), from a constants file the harness passes; recorded as `constants.how = "input"` with its SHA-256 |
543	   | Absys, SWI-Prolog, Python | **one marked constants block** in the program, between a line containing `CONSTANTS BEGIN` and a line containing `CONSTANTS END`, each inside a comment of the language, holding nothing but the constants, or **input**, as the system harness decides and documents; recorded as `block` or `input` |
544	
545	   A sub-problem with no constants (P04d, P04f, P08b; `variants/README.md`)
546	   records `none`. Sizes n and arrival orders are not constants (they are
547	   not varied) and come from the harness (point 3).
548	7. **Provenance** (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Writing a program", rules 1, 2, 8): its
549	   author, whether the author had seen a precursor, and the source of each
550	   idiom, in a comment the system harness README places.
551	
552	**H tokens** (`METRICS.md`, class H) are the per-system harness's own
553	calls as they appear in a program: the calls that pose stages, request
554	answers and print, the emit stub's binding, and output adapters (rule
555	13). Each system harness's README lists them, construct by construct,
556	before any program is written. Code a program adds beyond them is
557	classed by the rules of `METRICS.md`, not as H.
558	
559	## 12. What every system harness writes
560	
561	As its brief says (`sandbox/briefs/harness-system.md`), under
562	`harnesses/<system>/`: `run` with this command line for every
563	configuration and every mode the systems file allows, for every problem
564	P01–P16, spawn and the effects log included; `check CONFIGURATION
565	PROGRAM`, which executes nothing; a `README.md` with the program contract
566	of section 11 for its system, a complete minimal example for a made-up
567	problem, the H tokens, how it stops a system at the safety limit, whether
568	each configuration can continue after budget, and its confounds;
569	`S-mechanisms.md`; and `qualification/`, whose every record passes
570	`validate.py`. Anything it cannot do as this file says goes in its own
571	`QUESTIONS.md`, with the reading it implemented.
572

content.content:
# Protocol

*Draft 0.7.*

## Phases

1. **Draft.** `SPECIFICATION.md`, `METRICS.md`, this file and `problems/`
   are written. No program for the study is written, apart from the
   calibration programs (`METRICS.md`, Calibration), which are development
   examples and never results.
   Measurement may be qualified at this phase: establishing what each
   system can report, and adding instrumentation that changes no result,
   under the conditions in "Instrumentation" below.
2. **Independent review.** A reviewer who has not written the draft reads
   it for ambiguity, for errors in the valid outcomes, for language bias,
   and for problems missing from the suite. Findings and responses are kept
   in `reviews/`. *(Draft 0.1 had one review, answered in draft 0.2. Draft
   0.3 had a second, by a fresh reviewer, answered in draft 0.4. Draft 0.5
   had a third, answered in draft 0.6. Draft 0.7 is the freeze candidate.)*
3. **Freeze.** The specification is tagged `spec-1.0`, together with:
   - the pinned version or commit of every system in the first comparison;
   - each systems file's cores, flags and units;
   - the generic harness interface below.

   From then on, these change only by amendment.
4. **Harnesses.** One harness per system implements the interface, and is
   published before any program is run.
5. **Implementation.** Programs are written for each configuration from the
   problem files, one per configuration and problem, fixed before any of
   them is run.
6. **Results.** Each program is run and classified, and the results are
   recorded in `results/`.
7. **Comparison.** Only after results exist for at least two systems on
   every problem.

No system is implemented before the freeze. The benchmark is not changed
afterwards to suit any system, including PLANNER and the systems after it.

## Amendments

An amendment is a numbered, dated change to a frozen file, with its reason.
It applies to every system. Results obtained before it are kept, marked
with the specification version they were obtained under, and rerun under
the new version.

A problem proposed after the freeze does not join the frozen suite. It goes
into a separate, dated supplementary suite, reported apart from the frozen
one, with the date it was proposed and the results that existed then.

## Roles

| role | does | has access to |
|---|---|---|
| **specification author** | writes the problems and the protocol | the public repository |
| **variant custodian** | writes the hidden variants and their valid outcomes | the specification, and the private variants |
| **implementation author** | writes the programs | the public repository only |
| **harness author** | writes each system's harness (phase 4) | the public repository |
| **classifier A** | classes the programs' constructs, and the outcomes of every run on all axes, checking residual equivalence | the specification, the metrics, the programs, their outputs and the valid outcomes |
| **classifier B** | does both independently | the same, without A's classes |
| **verifier** | runs the programs on the hidden variants | the programs, the variants and their outcomes |

Each role is a separate agent or person, with its own context, and its
provenance is recorded. The two classifiers are of different origin (for
instance Claude and Codex), and neither wrote the program it classes.
Their disagreements, on tokens and on outcomes, are recorded, and a
disputed outcome is reported under both classes.

**Hidden variants** are made inaccessible, not merely placed where an
implementation author is told not to look. The custodian writes them
before the freeze and encrypts them with a key the project's owner holds
but does not use. The plaintext begins with a random nonce of at least 128
bits, so that a small space of constants cannot be recovered from its
hash. Only the ciphertext and the SHA-256 hash of the plaintext are
committed. The key is given to the verifier only after every primary
program and its results are committed. The verifier publishes the
plaintext, and anyone can check it against the hash. Each later wave of
systems (PLANNER onwards) has its own sealed set, made before that wave's
programs are written, since revealing a set publishes it.

## Evidence classification

Every implementation is given one or more of these classes:

| class | meaning |
|---|---|
| **original** | a surviving historical implementation, on the hardware or software it was written for |
| **rehosted** | a surviving historical implementation, running in a modern environment (an emulator, a port of the original source) |
| **reconstructed** | a modern implementation derived from historical documents, where no implementation survives |
| **modern** | a contemporary implementation of the language |
| **extended** | mechanisms supplied for the experiment, beyond the implementation's own |

Two qualifiers may be attached to a class:

- *with external mechanisms*: libraries or run-time features outside the
  configuration's core are used (`METRICS.md`);
- *alternative reading*: a reconstruction run with a decision taken the
  other way, where its sources conflict.

Results are always reported with the class. No result from a modern or
extended configuration is attributed to the historical language. Where a
language was described more fully than it was implemented (PLANNER and
Micro-Planner, for instance), the described language and the implemented
subset are separate systems.

## Configurations

A configuration is one system with a stated set of mechanisms. Results are
kept separate per configuration, so that a capability introduced later is
not attributed to the earlier model. Each systems file lists, per
configuration:

- its core, built-in by built-in;
- its flags;
- the unit of steps, of an alternative and of store, and how each is
  measured;
- what "the same computation" means. That is, whether a stage can be
  received into a computation already running, and how.

A reconstruction is pinned at a commit when the specification is frozen.
Any later change to it, for whatever reason, makes a new configuration,
reported separately, and never replaces the pinned one.

## Instrumentation

A measurement added to a system must not change what it computes. For a
reconstruction:

- the unmodified commit is kept as the baseline;
- instrumentation is made on a separate branch, and recorded as its own
  commit;
- it may not change scheduling, search, equality, suspension or any other
  rule of the machine;
- the instrumented build, with measurement on and off, must give output
  identical to the baseline's, byte for byte, on every example and in every
  output mode, including full traces. The check and its result are
  recorded.

## The harness interface

Every harness provides exactly these operations, and nothing that orders,
chooses or re-poses goals on its own:

- **pose(stage)**: give the system the information of one stage, into the
  same computation if the configuration allows it, or else by reposing.
  A reposed run replays **every** stage 1 to k in order, replacements and
  withdrawals included, and the program must carry them out. The harness
  never works out the net information itself;
- **spawn(computation)**: start a separate computation in the same
  instance (P09), returning at once where the configuration can run
  computations side by side. In a configuration that cannot, the first
  runs to its end or its budget, and then the next;
- **answers(cap)**: collect the answers the system reports, through its
  standard mechanism for enumerating them, until it is exhausted, the
  budget runs out, or `cap` answers have been collected. `cap` is 1 for an
  *any one* query and 20 otherwise, as each problem states. The execution
  state is classified after the call;
- **observe()**: record the state the common observations need, including
  bindings the system holds (`SPECIFICATION.md`, "reported");
- **print()**.

Each system's systems file says what its standard mechanism for answers
is. For Python and ALGOL 60, it is the values the program prints.

**Observing must not consume the computation.** In a system where
collecting answers would end or alter the computation that the next stage
extends (exhausting a backtracking search, for instance), the observation
of stage k is taken on a separate run of stages 1 to k. The incremental
run is left as it was.

**Commitments are preserved when a run is reposed.** When a commit stage
has selected an outcome v (P11), a reposed run replays it as the
information x = v. It does not ask the system to select again, which could
commit to a different outcome.

**External effects** (P11) are written to one log per problem, never reset,
across every run the harness makes for classification, reposed runs
included. Separate observation runs write to a separate log, which is not
judged. Entries that are duplicated only because a run was reposed are
counted separately, as the cost of reposing an irreversible effect.

Concurrency used to run computations (threads, processes) is a mechanism of
the configuration, listed in its systems file. A harness may not run
computations concurrently itself. In P09, all computations run in one
instance of the system, sharing one database, never in separate operating
system processes.

## Writing a program

1. Write it from the problem file. Programs written for this study's
   precursors (the absys experiments E01–E09) exist, and their author may
   have seen them; each program says whether its author had.
2. Use the idioms of the system's period where they are known. Cite the
   source of each idiom: a manual, a paper or a published program.
3. Transcribe the definitions given. Anything else is reformulation, and
   counts as R.
4. Where several idiomatic programs are possible, choose one per
   configuration and problem before any is run, or run and report every
   variant. In either case, one is designated the **primary** variant
   before any is run, and stands for the configuration.
5. **No anticipation.** The code that handles stage k may not depend on the
   content of any later stage.
6. **Genericity.** A program must stay correct when the constants in a
   problem's stages are changed. It keeps them in one marked place, or reads
   them as input, so that the verifier can substitute them. Each problem
   has hidden variants with other constants, held by someone who does not
   write programs. Every program is run on them after its results are
   recorded. The custodian works out each variant's valid outcomes
   independently, stage by stage, as the problem files give them for the
   original constants. A variant's outcomes need not have the same classes
   as the original's: other constants can make a finite outcome infinite,
   or a consistent stage inconsistent. A program's run on a variant is
   classified against **that variant's** valid outcomes, on the semantic and
   effects axes, exactly as a primary run is. A program **fails** a variant
   where that classification differs from its classification on the
   original constants, each against its own valid outcomes: a program
   complete on the original and unsound on the variant fails it. It is
   recorded as such, since it encodes a conclusion rather than computing
   it. The custodian records, for each variant, which of the original's
   outcome classes it was built to keep, if any.
7. A program may not be revised after its results are seen, except to fix a
   transcription error: a place where the program departs from the text of
   the problem file. Each fix is recorded as a diff, with the reason. A
   program changed for any other reason is a separate, named variant, and
   is reported as such.
8. Record the author of each program, human or agent.

## Running

- Pin the version of every system, and record its source and commit.
- **Budget.** 10⁶ steps in the system's own unit, per stage and per
  computation. In P09, each separate computation has its own budget and its
  own classification. A reposed run of stages 1 to k has a budget of its
  measured restart cost plus 10⁶.
- **The budget is relative to each system.** 10⁶ Absys steps, SWI-Prolog
  inferences and Python instructions are different amounts of work. So
  *budget* is a classification within a system, and is not compared
  across systems. Each system records, as a calibration figure, its steps
  for P13b at n = 10³, or, where P13b is not expressible, for P03e.
- **After budget.** If stage k ends in *budget* and the configuration can
  keep its computation and continue it, stage k+1 is posed into that same
  computation, with a new budget. Whether it can is recorded, since
  continuing past an exhausted budget is itself a capability. Stages 1 to
  k+1 are reposed only when the configuration cannot continue, and the
  reposing counts under restart cost.
- **After error.** Stage k+1 is posed by reposing stages 1 to k+1, counted
  under restart cost.
- **Safety limit.** A limit of 60 seconds per stage protects the harness.
  It is not a measurement. A stage it stops is rerun once, with the limit
  raised tenfold. If the rerun also stops, *timeout* is final for that
  stage. Both runs are recorded. Answers reported before the limit stopped
  the run are kept and classified on the semantic axis; only the execution
  state is *timeout*.

## Modes of running

Each program is run in up to three modes:

| mode | what it establishes | instrumentation |
|---|---|---|
| **behaviour** | the outcomes, the three axes and effects | none beyond the harness |
| **cost** | steps, answer latency, problem-defined operation counts | step counting only |
| **storage** | store, retained alternatives, suspended state | the systems file's storage measurement |

- The semantic result and execution state are taken from the behaviour run.
- Where two modes can be compared, their semantic results must agree, and
  any disagreement is reported as a fault of the instrumentation.
- A sampled measurement is never taken from the run that gives the step
  count or the classification, because sampling adds steps of its own.
- A run that hits the safety limit only because it is instrumented (in
  cost or storage mode, when the behaviour run finished) is not evidence
  that the model cannot complete the problem. It is recorded as a limit of
  the measurement.
- Run in CI where the system allows it, and compare with recorded output.

## Recording a result

Each result is a file `results/<system>/<configuration>/<problem>.md` that
gives:

- the specification version, the system version or commit, the
  configuration and the evidence class;
- the program, or a link to it at a commit, and whether its author had seen
  a precursor;
- for each stage, the common observations of `SPECIFICATION.md` and the
  problem's own;
- the token counts by class, per classifier, with the disputed tokens;
- the configuration's expressibility for the problem;
- the supporting code (S) used, by mechanism. An *extended* result is named
  by its mechanism. Every configuration's S mechanisms are listed, with
  their size, at phase 4, before any program is run;
- whether the program passed its hidden variants.

## Guarding against bias

- The reasons for choosing a problem, and the history of each system's
  implementation, are disclosed.
- Every review is asked for problems that favour designs other than those
  the suite came from.
- Results are reported for every system on every problem, including
  "not expressible".
- Both classifiers' token classes are kept and reported for every result,
  throughout the study, never only an adjudicated set. A comparative
  conclusion that would change if one classifier's classes were used in
  place of the other's is reported as **classification-sensitive**, with
  both figures.
- No ranking is computed. A summary may say where a system needed control,
  supporting code or intervention that another did not, and what it held in
  store to avoid them.
- Interpretation, including any connection to later work, is kept out of
  `results/` and in a separate document written after the comparison.
